archetypes.name: file-replacement-preservation
archetypes.rationale: The plan's Failure Mode 4 mitigation relies solely on updating compose_prompt() text in revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh, but extract_file_replacement_candidate() and validate_file_replacement() have no mechanism to detect optional trailers being silently dropped, and run_emit_plan_gate() exits 0 with legacy gating when trailers are absent — leaving the mechanical-churn exemption lost with no error signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/scripts/revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh` and focus on compose_prompt() (lines ~126-143), extract_file_replacement_candidate() (~398-452), validate_file_replacement() (~481-494), and run_emit_plan_gate() (~514-521). The plan asserts that updating compose_prompt() hard-rule prose is sufficient to ensure optional trailers (`diff_added`, `diff_deleted`, `mechanical_churn`) survive file-replacement revisions, but validate_file_replacement() only checks that the last non-blank line is `diff_lines: <N>` — it cannot detect silently dropped optional trailers in the lines immediately above that final trailer. After a tier-4 file-replacement win, run_emit_plan_gate() re-runs check-plan-size.sh via EMIT_PLAN; if optional trailers were dropped, that gate exits 0 using legacy diff_lines gating with no error, no warning, and no SOFT_ADVISORY signal — making the mechanical-churn exemption silently lost in every waterfall-revised plan. Verify whether the plan's proposed `test-revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh` regression can actually detect this silent degradation or whether it merely checks that a winning candidate eventually produces a valid `diff_lines:` tail, and confirm whether extract_file_replacement_candidate() or validate_file_replacement() also require changes beyond prompt text. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: trailer-scan-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The 'final contiguous metadata block' upward-scan stop condition is undefined for blank lines inside the block, the 'last full-line match wins for duplicate keys' rule is ambiguous about whether last-in-file-order means closest-to or farthest-from diff_lines:, and the PLAN_LINES subtraction edge case where a blank line between two optional trailers silently excludes the upper trailer from the count is absent from all proposed test cases.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/scripts/check-plan-size.sh` (lines 81-90 for current PLAN_LINES computation), `skills/design/scripts/check-plan-size.md`, `skills/design/scripts/test-check-plan-size.sh` (all existing cases), and the plan's 'Parse optional trailers only from the final contiguous metadata block' section. Verify that the upward-scanning stop condition is precisely defined for blank lines within the optional-trailer block: if a blank line appears between two valid optional-trailer lines (e.g., `diff_added: 100` at line 8, blank at line 9, `diff_deleted: 50` at line 10, `diff_lines: 200` at line 11), the scan starting at line 10 stops at the blank on line 9, which means `diff_added` at line 8 is treated as plan body and contributes to PLAN_LINES — but no proposed test case exercises this shape. Additionally, check whether 'last full-line match wins for duplicate keys' means last-in-file-order (closest to diff_lines:, encountered first in an upward scan) or last-encountered-in-upward-scan-order (farthest from diff_lines:), since the case 11 analogy sets 'last non-empty line in file wins' for diff_lines but does not disambiguate scan direction for keys within the optional-trailer block. Confirm whether the spoof-resistance test case explicitly tests that a prose line containing `diff_added: 0` below a blank line that separates it from the true final metadata block is correctly excluded from the subtracted count. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
